title: BFS and DFS
summary: Explore graphs and grids: breadth-first for shortest steps, depth-first for reachability.

questions.prompt: Same graph, depth-first. What does this program print?
In BFS, why mark a node as seen when it's added to the queue rather than when it's taken out?
options: Otherwise several neighbours can queue the same node before it's processed, wasting work

questions.prompt: BFS over a graph stored as adjacency lists, with V vertices and E edges. What is its time complexity?
Count the islands (connected groups of 1s) in a grid of 0s and 1s. Which approach?
options: Scan the grid; from each unvisited 1, flood-fill its island with BFS or DFS and count it
Binary search on the number of islands

questions.prompt: Put the steps of breadth-first search in order.
steps: Take the next node from the front of the queue
Put the start node in a queue and mark it seen
Add each unseen neighbour to the queue and mark it seen
Repeat until the queue is empty
